overall_summary: Extreme space anomalies and exoplanet survival scenarios are the primary growth drivers for FACTVERSE, consistently generating 5x to 10x more views than other topics. Conversely, generic psychology and repetitive animal facts struggle to gain traction.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Exoplanet Weather & 'What If' Survival Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,025 views), 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (643 views) are the top performers.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on highly visual, hostile planetary environments, framing them as hypothetical survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...').

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' was uploaded multiple times, peaking at only 53 views. 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' generated only 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Discontinue generic cognitive psychology facts and avoid recycling identical topics within short timeframes.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet in the Universe (TrES-2b)?
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a pitch-black screen and a heavy heartbeat sound effect, stating: 'If you fell into this planet, you would be plunged into absolute, terrifying darkness.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that despite reflecting less than 1% of light, the planet is actually a boiling 1,800°F gas giant that glows a demonic, faint red like a hot ember.
next_video.reason: TrES-2b is a proven high-performing topic (1,025 views). Combining it with the highly successful 'What If You Fell Into...' format leverages our best-performing hook structure.
